industry.headline: TikTok Settles Alabama Youth-Safety Lawsuit for at Least $100 Million Days Before Trial
industry.summary: TikTok settled with Alabama's AG for $100M-$300M and agreed to teen-safety features just before trial, the second major US settlement in weeks after Meta's $17.1B deal. State AGs are now extracting concrete behavioral guardrails (nighttime/school-hour limits, default privacy) from platforms, validating NOMO's off-social-media reward model and strengthening its pitch to US schools and prize sponsors.

industry.headline: Column: Meta's New Social Media Rules Should Have Started With Teens
industry.summary: Seattle high schoolers critique the rollout of Meta's court-mandated teen limits (2-hour daily cap, midnight-6am blackout, silenced school-hour notifications), noting no teens were consulted and none of the $237M-$339M Washington settlement money is earmarked for classrooms or parents. Reinforces that platform-imposed throttles are seen as porous and top-down, strengthening demand for third-party, reward-based tools like NOMO that schools and families can adopt directly.

reconsider.name: TikTok (Screen Time Rewards/Badges feature)
reconsider.reason: Duplicate of the TikTok Well-being badges candidate already included.
reconsider.why_fits: TikTok added badges and rewards for teens who avoid the app at night, stay within daily limits, and encourage others to participate — a direct gamification of reduced-usage behavior aimed at the same teen demographic NOMO targets.

reconsider.name: TikTok Well-being Rewards (badges for screen-time limits)
reconsider.reason: Duplicate of TikTok (in-app digital wellbeing rewards) entry
reconsider.why_fits: TikTok rolled out new features that let teens earn badges for avoiding the app at night, staying within daily limits, and encouraging others to participate — a social platform now gamifying reduced usage, directly competing with NOMO's reward-for-less-screen-time value proposition among the same teen audience.

reconsider.name: Timily
reconsider.reason: Mechanic (earning screen time via chores) is a weaker/different fit than NOMO's reduce-social-media-for-rewards model; medium confidence.
reconsider.why_fits: Timily is a newly prominent 2026 entrant built as a 'reward-first' system where kids earn coins for focus sessions, chores and challenges that unlock screen time or other rewards, directly overlapping with NOMO's gamified reduced-screen-time model for a youth audience.

reconsider.name: Go City (multi-attraction CityPASS-style passes)
reconsider.reason: Too similar to NOMO's existing GetYourGuide partner (city attraction/experience passes) without meaningful differentiation.
reconsider.why_fits: Go City sells all-inclusive city attraction passes (e.g., the Go City Philadelphia and Chicago passes covering dozens of top attractions), offering exactly the kind of tradeable, teen-friendly 'city green pass' reward inventory NOMO seeks, with a scalable commercial partner structure rather than a government dependency.

reconsider.category: Live entertainment / museum tickets for teens
reconsider.name: TDF (Tickets for Teens)
reconsider.reason: Duplicate of the higher-confidence 'TDF (Theatre Development Fund) - Tickets for Teens' entry covering the same program.
reconsider.why_fits: Theatre Development Fund runs a city-backed program giving NYC high schoolers free/low-cost Broadway, Off-Broadway, and museum tickets — a tradeable, teen-specific reward inventory analogous to NOMO's existing Fever/Ticketmaster partners, and newly expanded in summer 2026 with the NYC Mayor's office.

reconsider.name: U.S. Marshals Museum Youth Admission Program
reconsider.reason: Niche single-venue reward, redundant with Met Explorer Membership, medium confidence
reconsider.why_fits: A newly launched program (sponsored by Mercy) offering free general admission every Saturday through 2026 for visitors 17 and younger, a realistic, tradeable museum-ticket reward that fits NOMO's teen/Gen Z rewards inventory.

reconsider.name: NYC Department of Education / NYC City Council (DOHMH, DYCD)
reconsider.reason: Overlapping/duplicate of the more concrete, funded NYC Mayor's Office cell-phone-policy candidate; this one is just a hearing with less concrete detail.
reconsider.why_fits: NYC Council just held a hearing after DOE issued new 2026-27 screen-time and AI guidance with strict grade-level device-use limits, and city agencies (DOHMH, DYCD) are actively exploring phone-use limits in youth programs — a direct entry point for NOMO's district and municipality GTM motions.

reconsider.name: Boys & Girls Clubs of America national partner network
reconsider.reason: Duplicate/lower-confidence version of the 'BGC Mindful' BGCA entry, which has more concrete evidence of partnership appetite.
reconsider.why_fits: BGCA just rallied a slate of national brand partners (Comcast, Charles Schwab, Michaels, Murphy USA) for back-to-school youth wellbeing programming, showing an active, structured openness to exactly the kind of brand/rewards partnership model NOMO would bring to the Faith-based & Youth Orgs vertical.

reconsider.name: Dallas Park and Recreation Department (Mayor's Summer of Safety initiative)
reconsider.reason: Duplicate of Dallas Park & Recreation Teen All Access Pass entry
reconsider.why_fits: Dallas Park and Recreation runs a Teen All-Access Pass program under the Mayor's Summer of Safety initiative, partnering with area museums/attractions to give teens free access — a live municipal model for exactly the kind of city-level, teen-engagement partnership and reward distribution NOMO could plug into.

rejected_today.reason: Not a true product/mechanic competitor — a school curriculum/procurement nonprofit rather than a screen-time reward app, weak fit vs. the app-block/rewards competitor bar.
rejected_today.why_fits: Nonprofit being tapped for a proposed $17M+ South Carolina statewide digital wellness initiative for public/charter school students, showing it is actively competing for the same school/EdTech and state-level procurement relationships NOMO targets.

rejected_today.reason: Duplicate of the same Rogers-Screen Break story captured via the YMCA candidate; region ('Other'/Canada) is weighted as exploratory-only versus the US-anchored YMCA framing.

rejected_today.name: Oscar Health ("Oscar Unlocks" rewards program)
rejected_today.reason: Redundant with the more concrete Capital Blue Cross insurance-wellness candidate; why_fits leans on generic industry-trend framing rather than a specific NOMO opportunity.
rejected_today.why_fits: Oscar just rolled out a 2026 gamified member rewards program ('Oscar Unlocks') letting members earn badges, perks and rewards, signaling health insurers are actively building gamified wellness-incentive infrastructure — a strong entry point for NOMO's Insurance GTM vertical (owner João) to plug teen/family screen-time rewards into an existing insurer incentive rail.

rejected_today.category: State/Municipal policy mandate creating school-device-management demand
rejected_today.name: New Jersey Department of Education (bell-to-bell device policy mandate, P.L.2025 c.195)
rejected_today.reason: Duplicate of the more concrete, higher-confidence NJ DOE Phone-Free Schools Grant Program candidate covering the same policy wave.
rejected_today.why_fits: New Jersey now requires all public boards of education to adopt and implement a bell-to-bell personal-device policy starting the 2026-27 school year, creating a state-level procurement wave for digital wellbeing/screen-time solutions that fits NOMO's Municipalities & States GTM vertical (owner Leo) and the 6-12 Education vertical (owner João) simultaneously.

rejected_today.name: BePresent
rejected_today.reason: Duplicate entry for the same company already kept as 'BePresent (Screen Detox Inc)' with a higher-confidence, more specific why_fits.
rejected_today.why_fits: Positioned in the digital-detox app category alongside Opal, Brick, One Sec and Forest, but differentiated by a social/friends layer plus earned rewards — closely mirrors NOMO's social-accountability + rewards approach and should be tracked as a competitive entrant.

rejected_today.name: NCAA Division I Conferences (e.g., America East Conference)
rejected_today.reason: Vague why_fits describing NCAA's own generic wellness messaging rather than a concrete partner signal; college-level audience is a weaker demographic fit than NOMO's core teen/high-school target.
rejected_today.why_fits: NCAA now runs interactive modules covering how student-athletes' online presence and social media use can bring unwanted attention and harm well-being, and individual conferences like America East already run dedicated mental-health/wellness campaigns for their athletes — a genuine gap versus NOMO's current empty GTM roster, since conference-level offices are exactly the kind of large-roster, coach/administrator-driven buyer described for the Youth Sports vertical but are not yet approached by any screen-time reward platform.
